claims.text: Reliance Disclaimer significantly increased the Appropriate Reliance Ratio on the LSAT task from 1.17 in Control to 1.62 (p=0.04).
Implicit Answer significantly increased Relative Self-Reliance on the LSAT task from 0.44 in Control to 0.63 (p=0.002).
Implicit Answer significantly decreased Relative LLM Reliance on the Numerical Estimation task at the WoA > 0.01 threshold from 0.91 in Control to 0.67 (p<0.001).
Participants demonstrated higher gains in confidence when making incorrect reliance decisions than when making correct reliance decisions on the LSAT task (p=0.02).

evidence.description: Reliance Disclaimer yielded an ARR of 1.62 compared to 1.17 in Control on the LSAT task, with permutation testing showing p=.04.
Implicit Answer achieved an RSR of 0.63 compared to 0.44 in Control on the LSAT task, with permutation testing showing p=.002.
At WoA > 0.01, Implicit Answer reduced RLR to 0.67 from 0.91 in Control on the Numerical Estimation task (p<.001).
Across all conditions on the LSAT task, participants showed greater positive changes in confidence for wrong reliance decisions than appropriate reliance decisions (p=.02).

methodologies.name: Two-Stage Randomized Online Experiment
methodologies.description: A pre-registered randomized experiment with 400 participants measuring task performance, reliance metrics (RLR, RSR, ARR), confidence calibration, and engagement time across two stage decision-making.

limitations.text: Existing LLM reliance interventions lack comprehensive evaluations of appropriate reliance in real users.
The experiment evaluated crowdworkers on Prolific in a controlled lab setting, which may cause participants to act more cautiously or hedge decisions compared to real-world deployment.
The study evaluated a single model (GPT-4o) and did not test interactive follow-up capabilities or other LLM conversational styles.
The chosen tasks relied on multiple-choice and numerical estimation formats rather than naturalistic open-ended generative tasks like writing or coding.

future_work.text: Evaluate LLM reliance interventions in naturalistic, open-ended, and long-term deployment settings.
Quantify the comprehension difficulty of reliance interventions and tasks to analyze their relationship to reliance behaviors.
